After the remand order dated 20th January 2023 passed by the Apex Court in Civil Appeal No.
4555/2023, the writ petition was listed before this Court on a number of occasions.
2. On last date i.e. 24th September 2025, we had passed a reasoned order thereby noting that there was material to infer that the amount had been This is a digitally signed order.

The hearing of the matter on the said date was deferred as Mr. Gaurav Sarin, Senior Counsel appearing for petitioner, intended to verify the documents which were placed on record by the Land Acquisition Collector ('LAC') which form part of the order of this Court dated 24th September 2025.

3. Today, during the course of hearing, again an adjournment has been sought on the ground that in the land acquisition reference proceedings taken up before the Additional District Judge Tis Hazari,
arising out of Award No. 1717/ 1964 decided on 27th March 2009, the duty was cast upon petitioner Rameshwar Singh Tanwar And Ors vs Uoi And Ors on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76343907/

sentences.text: to ascertain the deposit of the amount pursuant to the statutory mandate provided under Sections 30 and 31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
4. The fact remains that the said fact was well within the knowledge of petitioner and was not disclosed in the petition.

However, today during the course of hearing, a copy of the said order was brought to the notice of this Court by Mr. Sarin, claiming that subsequent to the said order, Right to Information ('RTI') applications were preferred by petitioner.
In response to the said RTI, the reply furnished by respondent indicated non-deposit of the amount of compensation.
5. According to him, he may be granted a short further time to prepare and address the issue.
6. The fact remains that our order dated 24th September 2025 is quite clear.

The Apex Court vide its order dated 20th January 2023, has narrowed down the issue to be considered by this Court to the extent of lapsing of acquisition under Sub-Section 2 of Section 24 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act of 2013).

We have already noted from the documentary evidence brought on record that the amount was duly deposited with the Reference Court.
8. Apart from above, the said fact was required to be ascertained by the petitioner, as can be inferred from the order dated 27th March 2009 passed in the reference proceedings.

9. Merely because petitioner has obtained certain information under Right to Information Act 2005,
regarding the non-deposit of the amount of compensation with the Reference Court, that by itself,
will not give leverage to petitioner to claim that the compensation was not deposited and that,
therefore, the acquisitions stood lapsed.
10.
However, upon insistence, we grant time of two weeks, by way of a last opportunity, to the petitioner to prepare and address the matter.
11. Copy of the order provided by the counsel for petitioner is taken on record.

12. List on 20th November,2025 with the understanding that no further adjournment shall be granted in any manner whatsoever.
13.
Order be
uploaded on the website of this Court.
NITIN WASUDEO SAMBRE, J ANISH DAYAL, J NOVEMBER 6, 2025/
